item.title: Indian Pharma Has Little Reason to Fear Trump
item.description: Indian pharmaceutical firms have spent decades supplying American patients with affordable medicines. That dominance will be difficult to challenge, despite President Donald Trump’s threat to impose steep tariffs on imported generic drugs.
item.dc:creator: Juliana Liu

item.title: Central bank digital currencies are no match for dollar stablecoins
item.description: Cryptocurrencies emerged in part as a protest against central banks flooding the global economy with money during the financial crisis 18 years ago. Bitcoin’s earliest proponents were cypherpunks and crypto-anarchists who saw the monetary authorities as agents of a surveillance state that had to be circumvented, if not toppled. item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: 2026 Midterm Primaries Are Showing a Voter Enthusiasm Gap
item.description: We’re near the end of the 2026 primary election season and the state of American democracy is looking — sigh of relief — better than expected.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: The DSA Needs to Broaden Its Appeal. Here’s How
item.description: When Angie Nixon, a newbie member of the Democratic Socialists of America, pulled off a double-digit victory this past week to become the Democratic Party’s US Senate nominee in Florida, it was surprising. But not half as surprising as the types of voters who supported the longtime union organizer over her establishment-backed opponent, Alex Vindman.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith

item.title: Moderate Democrats Need to Actually Challenge the Left’s Ideas
item.description: The tumultuous 2026 primary season has made at least one thing clear: Democratic centrists are pursuing a losing strategy in their struggle with the left. Until the moderates change course, they will remain on the defensive.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Brownstein

item.title: Everything Is Lord of the Rings Now
item.description: The year 2026 is shaping up to be a chapter straight out of Tolkien. But this time, Frodo, Gandalf and company won’t be there to save anyone.
item.dc:creator: Christina Sterbenz

item.title: Ukraine War: Putin Thinks Russia Can Win By Out-Suffering
item.description: It hasn’t been an encouraging week for Vladimir Putin. Amid strikes and counterstrikes with Ukraine, Russia threatened that the UK “will pay” for supplying its opponent with the drones that have allowed strikes deep inside his country. The chief economist of the country’s second-largest bank was sacked for saying that Russia cannot win a “war of attrition” and that it could prompt a social crisis.
